display.purpose: Shared opening heading with tablet/mobile reductions.

shadows.name: button-material
shadows.purpose: Subtle raised rim around an opaque gloss-banded button face; disabled and reduced-transparency states remove the outer shadow.

motion.name: action-transition
motion.purpose: Enabled product button pointer press scales to .98 outside keyboard focus; reduced motion removes it.

motion.name: row-transition
motion.purpose: Result-row background feedback; shared liquid-metal controls use the action transition.

motion.name: comparison-highlight
motion.purpose: External comparison picker only; not product navigation.

motion.name: liquid-ripple
motion.purpose: One contained radial ripple at the pointer-click position. Optional shader loads for fine-pointer mouse hover or the bounded ripple, then retains its canvas through a 180ms exit; quick re-entry cancels disposal and reuses the context. Keyboard, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-color activation stay static.

motion.name: button-shimmer
motion.purpose: Fine-pointer hover moves the conic rim spark across the button width and rotates it 270 degrees. Idle gloss and spark remain static; reduced motion removes the transition.

motion.name: liquid-material-fade
motion.purpose: Fade in only once the optional shader is ready; retain its canvas for the 180ms fade-out, cancelling disposal on rapid re-entry.

narrative.overview:
The approved Y2K Futurism / Soft Club world uses icy-blue acrylic enclosures, silver seams, pearl reading fields and cobalt controls. Material framing provides identity even with every hero empty. Conventional text and controls carry the task; the generated three-screen board is a critique reference, not interface artwork or a pixel-matching comp.

This records the implemented October 21 Stage 9 comparison, merging the prior provisional system. Disc Tray is the selected body; final hero artwork remains unselected. The shared material world supersedes Stage 4's separate typography/theme directions; those remain historical evidence. Body selection does not authorize production promotion, Stage 10 or deployment; retain v1–v5 and comparison history after selection.

The subsequent Disc Study exploration settles the aesthetic preference on incumbent v2 and the body choice on Disc Tray. Gatefold, Disc Tray and Liner Notes remain available for comparison. Four user-authorized existing generated originals are compared only in working Disc Tray demos at `/prototypes/disc-tray/artwork/{slug}`; the picker changes artwork while preserving discovery state. The original five previews and three body-comparison routes retain flat placeholders.
keyCharacteristics: Five distinct app structures with shared Manrope typography, content and behavior.
Sculpted enclosure lips around near-opaque reading fields.
Liquid-metal button rims and static conic highlights around glossy opaque icy or cobalt faces, with bounded pointer motion.
Flat CSS hero reservations in original comparisons; four local decorative images only in the authorized Disc Tray artwork demos.
Native controls, visible keyboard focus and task-first mobile flow.
Persistent demonstration labels and an explicit real-data boundary.

rules.name: The Reading Field Rule
rules.body: Keep reading regions near-opaque; text must never depend on artwork for contrast.

rules.name: The Shared Voice Rule
rules.body: Keep Manrope and its loaded 500/600 weights across all five structures; structural differences must carry the comparison.

rules.name: The Task Before Hero Rule
rules.body: Put search and starting choices before decorative media on narrow screens; remove the reservation from working states.

rules.name: The Selective Chrome Rule
rules.body: Use reflective seams at enclosure and button boundaries while keeping reading faces, fields and result lists calm.

dos: **Do** retain all five structures, routes and comparison history until and after the user's structure selection.
**Do** keep shared Manrope typography, near-opaque reading fields, cobalt actions and selective enclosure chrome.
**Do** reuse the shared glossy liquid-metal button material with opaque reading faces, static idle highlights, bounded pointer feedback and static keyboard/fallback behavior.
**Do** preserve each original comparison's flat hero fill, aspect, location and future fit mapping, with task-first mobile order; keep the four artwork demos in Disc Tray's existing 1:1 slot.
**Do** preserve native controls, visible focus, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-color treatments.
**Do** label demonstration fixtures persistently and keep real failures separate from demo data.
**Do** treat review/capture evidence as scoped evidence, not deployment, user research or full accessibility conformance.
donts: **Don't** add artwork beyond the four user-authorized existing generated originals in the Disc Tray artwork demos; keep original comparison routes artwork-free and exclude reference screenshots, runtime remote images, illustrated substitutes and interactive hero controls.
**Don't** replace structural differences with typography/theme swaps or reserve blank hero space in working screens.
**Don't** turn approved glass/chrome into a generic ban or extend translucency into low-contrast reading regions.
**Don't** treat Disc Tray body selection or the artwork demos as authorization for production promotion, Stage 10 or deployment; final hero artwork remains unselected.
**Don't** inflate catalog, link, model-quality or personalisation claims beyond PRODUCT.md and frozen evidence.
